clue.text: A gem looks right in a ring

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation for right sits inside the word for a ring of bells

parts.note: a peal is a ring of church bells

explanation.surface: A jewel appears to sit perfectly in its ring setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looks' is a link meaning 'appears as'; a peal of bells is a ring, and R goes in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lustrous bead formed in an oyster is a classic precious stone.

clue.text: Article getting serious towards the end

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
stern means grave or serious

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece takes a grave turn in its closing paragraphs.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, the nautical term means at or towards the back, the rear end of the vessel.

parts.note: a firm's employees are its staff
a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: Workers drive along the ring road on their way into town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take' is a link. STAFFORD is the county town of Staffordshire in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an English county town, so a particular example of a town.

indicators.note: we hear tells us the travelling word is only matched in its spoken form

parts.note: travelling by a sledge over snow is sleighing

explanation.surface: Someone is killed while riding a sledge across the snow.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispatch a victim is to kill them, so dispatching means killing.

parts.note: to watch is to observe
to dog someone is to follow them closely

explanation.surface: A self-appointed crime fighter keeps an eye on someone and tails them.
explanation.definitionFit: A guardian who keeps a vigilant eye out for wrongdoing is a vigilante figure, a self-appointed guardian.

clue.text: The point of this device may not be apparent

definitions.text: The point of this device may not be apparent

parts.words: The point of this device may not be apparent
parts.note: a fastener whose sharp tip is tucked away under a guard, so its point cannot be seen

explanation.surface: A gadget whose purpose is hard to grasp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' looks like purpose, but it is the literal sharp tip, which this clasp hides under a cover.
explanation.definitionFit: The clasp's design hides its sharp tip inside a sheath so nobody gets pricked.

indicators.note: to group things is to arrange them, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A family full of gifted members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'group of' looks like a collective noun but signals rearranging RELATIVES.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone talented in many fields is described as adaptable and all-round.

clue.text: Paddle vessel plying to and fro

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A small boat is rowed back and forth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plying to and fro' says the word reads the same both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a light canoe propelled with a double-bladed paddle.

parts.note: ... water from a well or lifting something by hauling it up

explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upward' also hides WARD read upwards, a bonus hint.
explanation.definitionFit: To haul something up, such as a bucket from a well, is to pull it.

parts.note: an eco-minded bug, read as an ecological adjective followed by a winged pest

explanation.surface: A bug that cares about the planet.
explanation.definitionFit: The aphid is a garden pest whose name splits into an eco-friendly word and a winged bug.

definitions.meaning: a tennis or squash bat, taken out of its cover for use on court

explanation.definitionFit: A dishonest money-making scheme, and also the strung bat players wield on tennis courts.

definitions.meaning: to unfasten or open a knot or button
to ruin or bring about someone's downfall

explanation.surface: Someone is vulnerable to losing.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to unfasten and to ruin someone utterly.

clue.text: No methods are without publicity in these times

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the word for methods goes around the advert

parts.note: ways are methods
an ad is a piece of publicity

explanation.surface: Modern methods all fail without advertising.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means at the present time, in the current age.

definitions.meaning: fox-hunters traditionally wear scarlet coats called pink

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in excellent health, and literally describes riders dressed in hunting scarlet.

clue.text: Clued in a way to take one in

indicators.note: in a way says the letters are put in a different way, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A setter hides a word in a clue to fool a solver.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit someone into a group or count them is to take them in.

clue.text: One is not expected to live on them

definitions.text: One is not expected to live on them

parts.words: One is not expected to live on them
parts.note: a person near collapse or death is said to be on these final limbs

explanation.surface: Something too meagre to survive on.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being close to exhaustion or death; someone in that state may not survive.

indicators.note: in embarrassment says the letters are thrown into disarray

explanation.surface: Someone is bending over awkwardly in shame.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means vexation or mortification at failure or humiliation.

clue.text: Beaten by Noah's son and only daughter

parts.note: Ham was one of Noah's three sons in Genesis
mere means only or nothing more than

explanation.surface: Someone was thrashed by one of Noah's sons and his only girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal that has been struck repeatedly is beaten, and the word also means soundly defeated.

indicators.note: written about says the letters are set down in a jumbled order

parts.note: the possessive s is counted as a letter here

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor has penned a piece about a medication.
explanation.definitionFit: Anabolic compounds used by athletes are a class of drug.

definitions.meaning: made of the timber of a particular tree

explanation.surface: A carved toy horse, perhaps the one at Troy.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree yielding timber, and a reddish-brown colour of horse.

clue.text: It may be held in revulsion

definitions.text: It may be held in revulsion

parts.words: It may be held in revulsion
parts.note: faced with a bad smell, people pinch this part of the face shut

explanation.surface: Something regarded with disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: People hold this facial feature closed against a foul smell.

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a university degree, and the plural gives two of them
MA, Master of Arts, is a university degree, and the plural gives two of them

explanation.surface: A dam is constructed gradually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dam' is not a barrier but a mother, as in livestock breeding; 'gets built by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A dam is an animal's mother, and this is a childish word for mother.

clue.text: Might number clues in the wrong order

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a number

indicators.note: in the wrong order says the letters of clues are shuffled

explanation.surface: A setter may have numbered the clues out of sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: Physical strength or might is brawn.

clue.text: A reason why some people fight

definitions.meaning: a ground or motive for something
a principle or movement people campaign or battle for

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a reason for something, and also a principle that people struggle for.

definitions.meaning: magic charms, plural in the answer

explanation.definitionFit: The word means short periods of time, and also magic incantations.

clue.text: It may control the oven, cooking the roast

indicators.note: cooking the books means falsifying them, so the letters are altered

explanation.surface: An oven dial set while a joint is roasting.
explanation.definitionFit: A variable resistor regulating current, which can set a heater's power.

clue.text: They're not expected to impede one's progress

definitions.text: They're not expected to impede one's progress

parts.words: They're not expected to impede one's progress
parts.note: unforeseen obstacles or hitches that crop up and hold one back

explanation.surface: Things that ought not to slow someone down.
explanation.definitionFit: Unexpected obstacles or hitches that hold up progress.

parts.note: a life sentence is the longest prison term
a class is a category

explanation.surface: A permanent grouping of art students.
explanation.walkthrough: A life class draws from a nude model.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of art students drawing from a live model is so named.
